headline: Record quarter, margins expand, full-year guidance raised
summary_short: AMETEK posted record Q2 sales of $2.04B (+15% y/y) with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.77 (+14% y/y) and adjusted diluted EPS of a record $2.09 (+17% y/y); the company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $8.20-$8.30 from $7.94-$8.14.
summary_long: Revenue reached a record $2.04B (+15% y/y), with both segments growing double digits: Electronic Instruments +14% to $1.32B and Electromechanical +17% to a record $723M. GAAP operating income was a record $528M (26.6% adjusted margin, +60bp y/y); adjusted operating income rose 18% to $544M. Operating cash flow grew 35% to $484M; free cash flow conversion was 111% of net income. Net income rose 14% y/y to $407M; GAAP diluted EPS was $1.77 and adjusted diluted EPS a record $2.09 (+17% y/y). Orders grew 28% for a second straight quarter. Management raised FY2026 guidance: sales now expected up ~10% y/y, adjusted diluted EPS to $8.20-$8.30 (from $7.94-$8.14), and initiated Q3 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.08-$2.10.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited strong organic sales growth, contributions from recent acquisitions and outstanding operating performance driving high-teens adjusted earnings growth and 110bp of core margin expansion; orders grew 28% for the second consecutive quarter.

Growth was balanced across both segments: Electronic Instruments +14% y/y on organic growth plus acquisitions, with orders strength in semiconductor and commercial aerospace; Electromechanical +17% y/y (record) on strong organic growth with orders strength in medtech, defense and automation.

Adjusted operating income rose 18% as EIG core margins expanded 40bp to 30.1% and EMG core margins expanded 290bp, both attributed by management to strong operating performance; GAAP figures also carry acquisition-related integration costs not present a year ago.

Not explained in the release; the filing does not attribute the y/y cash decline to a specific use of funds beyond the disclosed operating, investing and financing activity in the cash-flow statement.
Not explained in the release beyond the balance-sheet reclassification of long-term debt into the current portion; no specific driver for the y/y increase is disclosed.
